Its statements about legal scholars contesting the boast and a broader pattern of legal failures are separate claims and need independent sourcing.
corrected_draft.description_long: The Washington Post’s January 2, 2019 article documenting Trump’s claims of expertise across different subjects reports that he made the courts statement at a rally in Texas in November 2015. The article quotes him saying, “I know more about courts than any human being on earth. Okay?” The supported event is the public boast, with the underlying event date in 2015 rather than the held record’s generic 2019 date. The article frames the remark as one example in a list of claims Trump made about his knowledge of various topics; it does not substantiate the held record’s assertions that legal scholars and constitutional law professors publicly contested this specific statement. Nor does this source establish the entry’s broader commentary about litigation losses or legal misjudgments. A corrected record should attribute the words, identify the rally date and location at the level the source provides, and omit those additional claims unless sourced separately.

corrected_draft.title: Trump Grants Steve Bannon Clemency in Final Hours
corrected_draft.description_short: Trump granted Steve Bannon clemency on Jan. 19, 2021, while Bannon faced We Build the Wall-related federal charges and had pleaded not guilty.
corrected_draft.description_medium: Reuters reported that Donald Trump granted clemency to Steve Bannon during a wave of pardons and commutations in his final hours on January 19, 2021. Bannon had been charged with defrauding supporters who donated to the We Build the Wall effort and had pleaded not guilty. DOJ’s clemency list identifies conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering. The claim about whether Bannon filed a clemency petition is not established here.
corrected_draft.description_long: On January 19, 2021, in the final hours of his presidency, Donald Trump granted clemency to former White House aide Steve Bannon as part of a larger group of pardons and commutations. Reuters reported the grant on January 20 and described Bannon as having been charged the prior year with defrauding supporters who contributed to a private effort to build a border wall; he had pleaded not guilty. The Justice Department’s clemency list names Bannon and identifies conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering. These sources support a discrete clemency action before the federal case reached trial. They do not establish whether Bannon submitted a petition through the Office of the Pardon Attorney, so the record should not assert that no petition was filed. It should also attribute the fraud allegations to the pending charges and avoid treating them as a conviction.
